A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PGA work, with readable text, equations, six figures and four tables supporting reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains the supplementary appendix referenced in the text; these judgments cover the supplied material.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original CARLA simulations, component ablations, toy-car experiments and a real-car physical attack, with quantitative and qualitative outcomes.

after.justification: Section 5 retains these original simulation, ablation and physical-experiment results, including Tables 1–4 and the real-car detection results.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same reconstruction, rendering and attack pipeline, surface-consistency measures, zero-order spherical-harmonic optimization, background min-max procedure and regularized objective.

E1.justification: Both report the same vehicle-detection coverage: CARLA scenes, a 1:24 Audi Q5 model and a full-size GOLF Sportsvan. References to supplementary infrared and full-coverage experiments are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains DAS, FCA, DTA, ACTIVE, TAS and RAUCA. Tables 2 and 4 retain FCA, DTA, ACTIVE and RAUCA. Changed citation numbers and newly cited background papers do not alter evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Both retain AP@0.5, the same four COCO-pretrained detectors, Faster R-CNN white-box optimization and transfer evaluation. Weather conditions, distances, pitch angles, angular sampling and reported image counts are unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 3 retains the same consistency/min-max ablation. Distance, weather and pitch-angle comparisons and the physical case studies are unchanged; no additional analysis appears in the supplied PDFs.

E5.justification: Both report point estimates and averages across conditions. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and the qualitative figures retain identical results. For example, PGA's Table 2 average remains 6.73, its Table 4 averages remain 28.69 and 28.26, and real-car AP@0.5 remains 88.48 clean versus 25.67 attacked.

T1.justification: The Gaussian definition, detection loss, min-max formulation, regularizers and update equations (1–14) are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about the first 3DGS-based physical attack framework, cross-view robustness, superiority to prior methods and infrared applicability.

C2.justification: Explanations of occlusion, background robustness and component benefits are unchanged, as are the rationales for partial camouflage and restricted evaluation distances and angles. No substantive limitation or qualification is added.

D1.justification: Acquisition and segmentation details, the 282 real-car reconstruction images and the advertised code link are unchanged. No implementation, hyperparameter, hardware, runtime or resource-access information is added.

R1.justification: Sixteen references are added and SegPGD is removed, increasing the bibliography from 51 to 66 entries. Additions include adversarial-transferability, watermark, vision-language and tracking work, mainly expanding introductory citation lists; Section 2's substantive comparisons and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Citation lists, reference numbering and the arXiv version/date header change. The scientific prose, terminology, section sequence and explanatory structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Expanded citations cause limited early-page text reflow, and the enlarged bibliography changes the layout of pages 9–11. All six figure images and four table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The broader bibliography adds little explanatory synthesis and introduces poor citation-context matches visible from the listed titles: v2 cites concealed-scene understanding [9] for natural-language processing and X-ray prohibited-item detection [38] for remote sensing. This modestly weakens citation precision, while the methods, experimental evidence and scientific explanations remain unchanged.
